correctness.rationale: The graph is explicitly specified by incidence equations over F_3 and crosschecked against a published LCF presentation by a 18-vertex bijection. All distances are computed exhaustively, proving exactly six 3-point forbidden blocks at threshold 3. The join identification proves the integral augmentation-tensor homology; graded symmetry gives the block sign and character product formula. A complete 3313-node backtracking search lists exactly 216 distance-preserving permutations; the 216 traces from the tensor formula agree element-by-element with independent oriented-face Lefschetz traces on all 4095 simplices. Character sum 216 gives 1 rational invariant. The orbit sum of a pure tensor has exact coefficient gcd 12, and division yields a nonzero 42-term vector with unit coefficients, checked fixed under every automorphism; therefore it is an integral primitive generator. Barycentric rational transfer gives the quotient Betti statement. The standalone verifier and saved output reproduce these finite checks; no experimental extrapolation is used.

value.rationale: The Pappus graph is a natural high-symmetry Levi graph. Its rank-64 homology is already known nonequivariantly, but the full 216-element signed integral action is new structural information: its full fixed subgroup is a single primitive Z-class while the 108-element part-preserving subgroup fixes rank 3. This yields nonvanishing rational fifth homology in the topological quotient and explicitly identifies an integral invariant representative, not inferable from the nonequivariant wedge count. The question is directly motivated by equivariant Rips homology and the graph's canonical automorphism group.
